body.description: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a transformative photovoltaic technology. However, the device performance of inverted PSCs is dramatically limited by surface defects and the underlying film morphology of metal halide perovskite (MHP) thin film. Herein, we report a novel buried interface layer consisting of SiO<sub>2</sub> nanoparticles (NPs) chemically bonded to graphene oxide (GO), deposited atop a hydrophobic hole extraction layer (HEL) to address this limitation. The SiO<sub>2</sub> NPs serve as insoluble scaffolds that immobilize GO sheets on the hydrophobic HEL surface, enabling the formation of homogeneous MHP thin films. Meanwhile, the GO functional groups interact with surface-uncoordinated Pb<sup>2+</sup>, suppressing interfacial defects and guiding crystal grain growth of the resultant MHP thin films. This synergistic effect suppresses non-radiative charge recombination and enhances charge extraction efficiency. As a result, a 26.07% efficiency with significantly suppressed photocurrent hysteresis is observed from PSCs incorporating the SiO<sub>2</sub>-GO buried interface layer. Moreover, the above PSCs maintain 92% of their initial PCE after 1800 h of continuous operation at the maximum power point under AM 1.5 G (100 mW/cm<sup>2</sup>) illumination at 25 degrees C in air with 50-60% relative humidity. These results demonstrate that we have developed a facile and effective way to realize high-performance inverted PSCs.
body.title: Reducing non-radiative recombination in perovskite solar cells with a SiO<sub>2</sub>-graphene oxide buried interface layer

body.description: We investigate the nanoscale function of additives used for tin-containing perovskites, using the archetypal FASnI<sub>3</sub> (FA = formamidinium). First, we find that the addition of sodium borohydride (NaBH<sub>4</sub>) is inhomogeneous, with 200–500 nm aggregates forming on the FASnI<sub>3</sub> surface. The inhomogeneous distribution of NaBH<sub>4</sub> leads to a relatively small (∼1% of the film) amount of reduced perovskite, but the macroscopic properties are dominated by the overwhelming space without any treatment. Upon illumination, more aggregate regions (∼13%) become activated due to reduction of photogenerated I<sub>2</sub>. On the other hand, when we combine NaBH<sub>4</sub> with dipropylammonium iodide (DipI) passivation and illuminate, we observe a much more homogeneous activation effect, which we attribute to denser coverage of NaBH<sub>4</sub>. We find that the iodine content in FASnI<sub>3</sub> films treated with NaBH<sub>4</sub> and DipI is 64% less than in those treated with NaBH<sub>4</sub> alone. These results underline that the microscale configuration of different additives in tin perovskites is deeply interconnected and it is essential to uncover their chemical reactivity.
body.title: Direct Microscale Observation of Additive-Triggered Reduction in Tin Halide Perovskites

body.description: Effective interfacial passivation is essential for achieving high-performance perovskite photovoltaics. 2D/3D heterostructures are a widely adopted strategy for defect passivation and band alignment regulation. Despite recent progress, achieving favorable interfacial energetics and comprehensively suppressing nonradiative recombination at both surfaces and grain boundaries continues to be an active area of investigation. We introduce a coassembled 2D architecture in which long-chain ligands are complemented by a minority component of short-chain ligands to form a mixed-ligand passivation layer. Such a coassembled structure promotes preferentially phase-pure, n = 2, 2D layer formation, resulting in an energetically favorable band alignment that enhances charge extraction. In addition, this coassembly facilitates effective passivation of interfacial defects at both surfaces and grain boundaries, leading to suppressed nonradiative recombination. As a consequence, these interfacial improvements increase carrier lifetimes and enhance the fill factor and open-circuit voltage of the device, yielding a higher power-conversion efficiency.
body.title: Mixed-Ligand-Driven Phase-Pure 2D Perovskite for Interfacial Passivation of Perovskite Photovoltaics

body.description: The commercialization of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) faces significant challenges due to their sensitivity to environmental humidity, which compromises film crystallization and device stability. Here, we introduce diphenylvinylphosphine (DPVP) as a Lewis base additive that enhances the performance and reproducibility of PSCs fabricated under ambient-air conditions. DPVP suppresses moisture-induced defect formation and stabilizes crystallization within realistic process-humidity ranges (20–40% relative humidity) commonly encountered in laboratory and pilot-scale manufacturing environments. It improves film uniformity, reduces trap densities, and yields highly reproducible device performance, enabling champion PCEs of 24.2% in small-area devices and 20.5% in blade-coated 12 cm<sup>2</sup> mini-modules. Furthermore, DPVP-assisted modules exhibit enhanced stability, retaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 900 h of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) at 65 °C. This study demonstrates a humidity-resilient and scalable additive strategy for ambient-air perovskite photovoltaic manufacturing.
body.title: Molecular Additive Engineering for Process-Humidity Robustness and Reproducible Fabrication of Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules

body.description: The interplay between carrier density regimes and the various scattering processes is fundamental for understanding charge transport efficiency in high-performance semiconductors. Combining ultrafast time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS) and transient microwave photoconductivity (TRMC), we measure carrier mobilities over 7 orders of magnitude (10<sup>13</sup>–10<sup>20</sup> carriers cm<sup>–3</sup>), reaching a regime where carrier–carrier scattering dominates and mobility begins to roll off. We find the Caughey–Thomas model can be effectively employed for transport modeling in 3D metal halide perovskites (MHPs), and the mobility roll-off near ∼10<sup>19</sup> cm<sup>–3</sup> can be tuned by MHP composition. Carrier lifetime in MHPs starts decreasing at much lower carrier densities due to interband multi-carrier recombination, while intraband carrier mobility remains unchanged as carrier–carrier scattering is screened by the presence of polarons. The validated Caughey–Thomas model provides a practical input for device simulations, prevents overestimation of diffusion length under high injection, and suggests that MHPs are excellent candidates for unipolar device applications under high carrier densities.
body.title: Large Polaron Screening Delays Mobility Roll-Off in Halide Perovskites under High Injection
